citations.title: Agentic CAD According to Engineers Building It
excerpts: # What Is Agentic CAD? We Asked CoLab Engineers Building AI for CAD
Agentic CAD is more than text-to-CAD demos. Two engineers building AI for CAD explain what it can do, where it fails, and what comes next.

Agentic CAD has moved quickly from niche research topic to engineering buzzword. It is showing up in vendor announcements, AI demos, product roadmaps, and conversations about the future of mechanical design. It is also one of the fastest-moving categories in the broader landscape of [AI tools and agents for mechanical engineers](https://www.colabsoftware.com/ai-tools-for-mechanical-engineers-guide) .
Most of that attention is focused on one question: **Can AI create CAD geometry from a prompt?** For engineering teams, creating geometry is only the starting point. The hard part is what comes next.

Once [generated CAD (genCAD)](https://www.colabsoftware.com/guides/how-generative-design-works-a-guide-for-engineering-managers) exists, engineers still have to answer many questions that decide whether it can move forward. Can the model be edited in the team’s CAD system? Can it be manufactured at the required volume and cost? Can another engineer understand how it was built?

To date, credible answers to those questions have been few and far between. To help clarify what agentic CAD is and what opportunities exist, we asked two engineers who have built real products and real AI tools for engineers.

[Shahed Saleh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shahed-saleh/) is a Senior Product Manager on CoLab’s AI team. She is a mechatronics engineer by training, with prior experience building AI-enabled industrial inspection systems at DarwinAI and research roles in additive manufacturing and robotics at the University of Waterloo.

[Jeremy Andrews](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeremyandrewscolab/) is CoLab’s CTO and Co-Founder. He is a mechanical engineer who ran DFM reviews on Tesla Model 3 battery pack components and at General Dynamics before co-founding CoLab in 2017. He has spent the nine years since building software that reads, renders, and processes native CAD data across 30+ file formats.
We asked Shahed and Jeremy what agentic CAD is, where it works today, where it falls short, and what engineering leaders should expect over the next year and beyond.
Agentic CAD is AI taking goal-directed action inside a geometric design workflow.

The “agentic” part is the difference between advice and execution. A chatbot can [answer a question about CAD or suggest what an engineer should click next](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/ai-agents-for-engineering-vs-chatgpt) . An agent can actually drive the CAD tool itself. It builds or edits the geometry, checks the result against requirements, and iterates until it gets there. This workflow is distinct from purpose-built CAD-generation models.

**‍** I think there are a few different categories getting grouped together right now. One is full text-to-CAD. That is probably the flashiest version, where you prompt a chatbot or a model and it produces CAD data on the other side.

A lot of that work has historically been less about mechanical CAD for product manufacturing and more about 3D models for visual use cases, like animation, video games, or sometimes 3D printing. In those cases, the output may be a mesh or another kind of 3D representation, but not necessarily the kind of parametric CAD data [our customers](https://www.colabsoftware.com/customers) work with.
There are also people working on text-to-CAD for parametric models. That work is interesting, but it still seems early.

The other category is using agents to automate existing CAD tools. The [Autodesk and Anthropic Fusion MCP](https://www.colabsoftware.com/post/autodesk-fusion-mcp-faster-cad-same-bottleneck) example fits there. That path is probably closer to what actually gets adopted, at least in the medium term, because it works with the CAD tools and file formats companies already use.

Useful production use cases today are bounded and lower stakes. This might include CAD documentation copilots, retrieval across file vaults or PLM, repetitive parametric edits in CAD tools, first-pass concept geometry, and [review triage that flags issues for an engineer to correct](https://www.colabsoftware.com/product/ai-cad-review) .

basis.reasoning: The blog index identifies a CTO-authored article about building AI-powered DFM checks. A second CoLab engineering article is by its CTO and an AI-team product manager and discusses agentic CAD’s technical operation and limitations, supporting the presence of at least two technical posts by product engineers.

citations.title: Job Application for Manager, Revenue Operations Systems at CoLab Software
excerpts: The **Manager, Revenue Operations Systems** will be the technical backbone of CoLab’s revenue operations team. You’ll own the architecture, build, and integration of the tools and data model that Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success run on — and the reporting infrastructure that leadership uses to inspect the business.

This is a hands-on ownership role, not an oversight role. You’ll design the data governance architecture alongside the SVP of Operations and then build it yourself. You’ll partner closely with a Revenue Operations counterpart who owns process, hygiene operations, and rep-facing enablement, and you’ll be the technical depth behind that partnership.

+ Own the implementation, integrations, workflow design, and ongoing management of the tools serving the revenue organization, including CRM (Salesforce), business intelligence (Tableau), sales engagement (Salesloft/Outreach), CPQ and quoting, conversation intelligence (Gong), data enrichment (ZoomInfo), product analytics (Mixpanel), internal app building (Retool), AI assistants, and the Slack and Google Workspace integrations that connect them.
+ Ensure all systems are optimized for performance and scale with the business, and stay aligned to how revenue teams actually work.
+ Oversee integrations across the tech stack to ensure seamless data flow and functionality.
+ Own implementation and rollout once a tooling decision is made, including migration planning and cutover, partnering with IT on provisioning and security.
+ Develop and implement automation workflows to streamline revenue operations and measurably reduce manual work across Sales, Marketing, and CS.
+ Continuously evaluate systems for process improvement opportunities.

+ Own the Salesforce data model and the governance architecture that protects it: object and field design, validation rules, required-field and stage-gating logic, permissions, and record-type structure.

+ Design governance standards in partnership with the SVP of Operations, then build and maintain the enforcement layer that makes those standards hold — so data quality is structural rather than dependent on cleanup after the fact.
+ Partner with Sales Operations, who maintains governance standards day to day and drives the rep behaviour that keeps data clean inside the architecture you build.

+ Build and maintain the reporting layer that powers the revenue operating cadence: pipeline health views (stage and aging flags, at-risk identification, segment benchmarks), forecast and quota attainment reporting, and GRR/NRR views.
+ Ensure reporting is accurate, accessible, and trusted without rework, including at the SLT and board level, and document data definitions so the business shares one version of the truth.

+ Own the RevOps request queue: intake, triage, and prioritization of system, reporting, and data requests from across the revenue organization — balancing fast turnaround on transactional work against the architectural fixes that reduce the volume of requests over time.

+ Take on a standing backlog of systems debt, including enforcement gaps in the CRM (stage validation and required-field logic that doesn’t yet exist), price book consolidation and product SKU structure, field and product data that has drifted out of alignment, and manual provisioning workflows that should be automated.
+ Distinguish between requests that need a fix and requests that signal a structural problem, and make the case for the second when it’s the better use of time.
+ Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success to align system capabilities with business needs.
+ Provide training and assistance to teams on tools and best practices, and build reusable documentation and how-to assets.
+ Collaborate with Enablement to land system and process changes, anchoring them in how each team actually works day to day rather than in how the system is configured.

* Tooling evaluation and rollout: own evaluation end to end — requirements, technical and integration assessment, security review, and business case. Sales Operations co-owns the decision and owns commercial negotiation with vendors.

* Cross-functional project ownership: own operational initiatives that sit outside any single team’s ownership — for example a lead-to-close process audit across Sales and Marketing, or a reporting consolidation spanning CS and Sales — owning the project plan, stakeholder communication, and outcome, not just the technical execution.
+ 5+ years in revenue operations, sales operations, business systems, or a comparable systems-ownership role in B2B SaaS.
+ Track record as the primary owner of a revenue tech stack — not a contributor to someone else’s.

+ Deep Salesforce administration experience (Admin certification or equivalent): data model design, Flow, validation rules, permissions and sharing, and integration architecture. Apex or scripting experience is an asset, not a requirement.
+ Hands-on experience with Tableau or similar BI tools for advanced data visualization — dashboards the business relies on, not one-off reports.
+ Experience with a sales engagement platform such as SalesLoft or Outreach.
+ Experience integrating a revenue stack across tools, with an understanding of where data breaks between systems and how to prevent it.

+ Nice to have: CPQ or quoting configuration, Gong, ZoomInfo, Retool or similar low-code app building, Mixpanel or comparable product analytics, Chili Piper, Zendesk, HubSpot, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
+ Experience building revenue reporting: forecasting, quota attainment, pipeline health, and GRR/NRR.

basis.reasoning: The Trust Center says Salesforce manages customer and sales information and HubSpot is used for inbound sales and marketing. The RevOps posting names Salesforce, Salesloft/Outreach, Gong, and ZoomInfo in its revenue stack.

excerpts: # CoLab reveals broad vision for generative engineering, with release of generative artifacts to be quickly followed by generative CAD‍

Today, CoLab revealed its vision for generative engineering, announcing the release of a new capability called generative artifacts and setting a date for the launch of a generative CAD product in H1 2027.

St. John’s, NL, Canada (September 30, 2026) – Today, CoLab revealed its vision for generative engineering, announcing the release of a new capability called generative artifacts and setting a date for the launch of a generative CAD product in H1 2027.

“There is a lot of excitement about generative CAD accelerating design iterations and allowing engineering teams to explore more concepts,” said Adam Keating, Co-founder and CEO of CoLab. “It’s an important piece of the puzzle, but if all you do is speed up CAD operations, you’re not really solving for program speed. The question engineering leaders should be asking is not ‘how can I adopt generative CAD?’ but ‘how can our organization shift toward generative engineering?’”

Generative artifacts, a new capability from CoLab, provides one example of what generative engineering could look like in practice. Beyond CAD, there are dozens of other artifacts that engineering teams must mature and approve for release. Using CoLab, engineering teams will be able to generate and refine these artifacts – for example, a Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) or a root cause analysis – retaining critical program context, alongside the history of each design.

CoLab also revealed plans to release a generative CAD product in H1 2027. With model capability advancing rapidly, CoLab is focused on providing guardrails that will help AI produce outputs engineers can trust.
